minutes.headline: Commission approved Hickory Hills dam tree removal for dam-safety compliance; continued four hearings to Feb 18
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission continued four pending wetlands/flood-plain hearings (58 Spring St, 30 Summer St, 763 Northfield Rd culvert, 27 Fire Road) to February 18, with lengthy discussion at 27 Fire Road over a proposed no-build-zone waiver and a larger replacement house. The commission also heard Hickory Hills Lake's annual management report and approved removing trees near the dam toe for state dam-safety compliance, conditioned on replanting with native, pollinator-friendly plants, and discussed grant applications, a heating-invoice payment, and fee-structure and stormwater bylaw work in old/committee business.

what_happened.line: Commission approved removing trees near the Hickory Hills dam for state dam-safety compliance, on condition the area is replanted with native, pollinator-friendly plants.
Four pending wetlands and flood-plain hearings were continued to February 18, including a contested request to waive a no-build zone for a larger replacement house at 27 Fire Road.
A hearing on the town DPW's proposed culvert replacement at 763 Northfield Road was also continued to February 18.
The commission is holding off on revamping its fee structure and consultant fees until the new conservation agent starts on February 9.

why_it_matters: The dam-safety tree removal affects the shoreline around Hickory Hills Lake and comes with a replanting condition rather than leaving the area bare.
The 27 Fire Road no-build-zone waiver, still undecided, will shape how close a rebuilt house can sit to protected wetland; abutters and the applicant return February 18.
A revised commission fee structure could change what applicants pay for wetlands review once the new conservation agent is in place.
